Subject: Finlytics security/telemetry discovery — action items & docs

Hi Lily / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and the next steps so we can keep procurement moving: 

Summary
- Finlytics is evaluating Redwood for document summarization and embeddings for search across regulated LOBs.
- Key risk areas you flagged: SOC 2 status and timeline, GDPR data residency, HIPAA applicability for a subset of PII, and how the Console surfaces telemetry/cookies to end-users.

What Redwood confirmed on the call
- SOC 2: Redwood is in the middle of a Type II audit (controls in place; control testing window: Apr–Sep 2026). Expect preliminary report Q1 2027. We can provide our Type I and relevant control narratives now. (Karthik will follow up with the control matrix.)
- GDPR/HIPAA: We support data residency via dedicated clusters and have a HIPAA-ready config for covered processing (BAA available for customers).
- Telemetry/cookies: Console collects minimal product analytics (latency, error rates, feature usage) and uses a small client cookie for session settings; opt-out and data retention controls exist. Marissa will send the cookie matrix and docs link.

Attachments I’m sending in parallel
- FINLY-Security-SQ-Initial.pdf — a stubbed vendor questionnaire with fields you flagged.
- redwood-telemetry-cookie-matrix.xlsx — mapping of console cookies and telemetry events.

Action items (owner / ETA)
1) Fill initial SQ and return — Finlytics (Lily) — by 2026-11-13 if possible.
2) Deliver control narratives + SOC1/Type I artifacts — Karthik (karthik.iyer@redwood.com) — by 2026-11-12.
3) Share telemetry/cookie docs and a short explainer for privacy team — Marissa — today.
4) Schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive on SSO/BAA scope if needed — Aditya to propose slots for next week.

If there are other stakeholders who should be added (legal/privacy/security), please reply-all with names and we’ll loop them in.

Best,
Hannah

Hi Hannah —

Appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from Finlytics side: 

1) SOC 2 timing is important — our procurement requires a completed Type II report for production access. Will you confirm whether the preliminary report you mentioned includes any failed exceptions? We understand audits can have findings.

2) HIPAA: we have a subset of customers with PHI (claims-level metadata). Could you confirm that Redwood’s HIPAA-ready configuration supports encryption at rest with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)?

3) Cookies/telemetry: our privacy team wants the exact list of console cookies and whether any third-party trackers are loaded on the docs site (we use the docs to train our privacy counsel on platform behavior).

I’ll take a first pass on the questionnaire and get it back to you by Friday (2026-11-13). Also looping in Tom (@Tom) to propose a shortlist of internal reviewers (legal + infra) — Tom?

Thanks,
Lily

Subject: Console cookies + telemetry docs & quick explainer

Hi Lily —

Following Hannah’s note, attaching the telemetry cookie matrix and linking our public docs. Short answers up front: 
- No third-party ad trackers on the Redwood Console or docs site; we use Segment for event routing to internal analytics and a lightweight CDN analytics beacon for page views (both are configurable).
- Console cookies are scoped to session and preferences; none contain PII. Retention policies are configurable by account for telemetry aggregates.
- KMS/HSM: For Private and Dedicated deployments we support customer-managed keys for data at-rest encryption; in the hosted product we offer KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and can discuss HSM for enterprise agreements.

Please see the two attachments (redwood-telemetry-cookie-matrix.xlsx) and the public docs link below for the canonical cookie table. I called out the rows that Finlytics asked about.

Docs: https://docs.redwood.com/telemetry/cookies

If it’s helpful I can prepare a 15-min recording walking the privacy team through the sheet and where to find the control narratives in our compliance portal.

Best,
Marissa
